outcome: fetal complications (meconium-stained liquor, meconium aspiration syndrome, NICU admissions, perinatal asphyxia, hyperbilirubinemia)
cohort: 150 pregnant women with post-dated pregnancies beyond 40 weeks of gestation, excluding those with previous cesarean sections, congenital anomalies, malpresentation, multiple gestation, and specified medical conditions.
finding: The study found that 68% of post-dated pregnancies resulted in vaginal delivery (40% induced), 32% in cesarean section, and reported specific rates of maternal (e.g., postpartum haemorrhage 6.6%, perineal tears 4.6%) and neonatal complications (e.g., meconium aspiration syndrome 5.3%, NICU admissions 24.6%, perinatal asphyxia 2.6%, hyperbilirubinemia 2%).
mod_finding: 68% of participants had vaginal deliveries (40% induced) and 32% had cesarean sections, with induction at 40 weeks suggested to mitigate risks in prolonged pregnancies.
